A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts and appendices are available, and corresponding methods, tables, and figures can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual reasoning experiments, script-control accuracy comparisons, and Logit Lens analyses in Sections 4–6 and Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds script-percentage details and illustrative model outputs.

M1.justification: Language detection, script-constrained decoding, and Logit Lens analysis remain unchanged. Expanded correlation explanations document the existing analysis; adaptive language selection is proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six-language K&K coverage across seven difficulty levels and the same 15-language, 18-subject m-MMLU coverage. The new language/script table and Arabic examples document retained coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated models and backbone comparisons remain unchanged. The script-control comparisons retain R1-70B, R1-32B, R1-14B and the same control conditions in v1 Tables 8–9 and v2 Tables 10–11.

E3.justification: Model configurations, decoding hyperparameters, language-identification procedures, validity filtering, and evaluation metrics are retained. The added examples use existing script-control settings, while the correlation calculation is explained more explicitly.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2.2 adds a matched case study of one Arabic K&K puzzle under unconstrained, Latin, Han, and Arabic script conditions. Figures 11–14 provide qualitative evidence showing how script control affects reasoning outputs.

E5.justification: No repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practices are added or revised. Pearson correlation was already used in v1; v2 expands its explanation.

E6.justification: Existing accuracy, entropy, validity-rate, and correlation results are unchanged after matching tables and plots. v2 adds numerical script percentages across difficulty levels in Table 9 and concrete output examples in Figures 11–14.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs. The expanded Pearson-correlation explanation documents an existing calculation without adding mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's principal contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about language-mixing patterns, script-control benefits, and alignment between internal representations and reasoning traces.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds an implication for future work: learning to select reasoning languages adaptively at different stages. Existing result interpretations and the limitations concerning script-level control, training origins, language coverage, and R1-Zero remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 and new Appendix A.1.3 document the per-script, across-difficulty correlation calculation more explicitly. Tables 8–9 add language/script mappings and supporting percentages; existing model, hyperparameter, and translation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Liu et al. (2025), Nie et al. (2025), and Yan et al. (2025), supporting multilingual representation, language-confusion, and adaptive-strategy discussion. The main research positioning and novelty claim remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to expanded correlation explanations, a new appendix subsection, an additional discussion paragraph, example descriptions, and reference and author-contact edits. The overall section sequence and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds two explanatory tables and four boxed output-example figures, relocates Figure 7, and reflows appendix material. Existing plot graphics and numerical table formats are retained rather than broadly redesigned.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful procedural explanations, script mappings, and concrete examples. However, applying its stated calculation to new Table 9 gives Hindi R1-70B correlations of approximately 0.9180 for Latin and 0.9257 for Devanagari, whereas unchanged Table 4 reports 0.8875 and 0.9019. Both indicate strong associations, but the unexplained mismatch compromises the reproducibility clarification. These documentation gains and the unresolved inconsistency leave the net quality direction uncertain.
